sentences.text: The petitioner has stated in the Crl.M.C. that he is running a business in Thailand from 2015 onward.
The petitioner was totally unaware of the above proceedings.
It is only recently that the petitioner came to learn that a non- bailable warrant has been issued against him, i.e., when he went to renew his passport.
The petitioner is ready and willing to appear before the Trial Court and get himself enlarged on bail.

However, the petitioner is apprehensive that he may be arrested, while returning back to India and his application CRL.MC NO. 2577 OF 2026 2026:KER:27618 may not be considered on the date of surrender.

Hence, the Crl.M.C.
3. I have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor and the learned DSGI.

4. On a consideration of the facts and materials on record, I dispose of the Crl.M.C. in the following manner:
(i) It would be upto the petitioner to approach the 3 rd respondent and file an application for issuance of an emergency certificate.
If such application is filed within a period of two weeks, the 3 rd respondent shall consider the application and dispose the same in accordance with law.
(ii) On receipt of the emergency certificate, the petitioner is directed to return to India within a week from the date of receipt of the emergency certificate.
(iii) On arriving in India, the petitioner is directed to report before the Investigating Officer in Crime No.194/2015 of the Nallalam Police Station, Kozhikode.

(iv) The Investigating Officer is directed to obtain the CRL.MC NO. 2577 OF 2026 2026:KER:27618 phone number, address and the other details of the petitioner, and ensure that he surrenders before the Trial Court within a week from the date of his arrival in India.
However, the Investigating Officer shall not enforce the NBW.

(iv) On the petitioner surrendering before the Trial Court, and filing applications to recall the NBW and to enlarge him on bail, the Trial Court shall consider the applications, in accordance with law, on the day that the petitioner surrenders before the Trial Court.

(vi) In order to enable the petitioner to surrender before the Trial Court, the NBW issued against the petitioner shall be kept in abeyance for one week from the day he arrives in India, provided the petitioner appears before the Investigating Officer on the day he returns to India, and surrenders before the Trial Court within a week thereafter.
